dedupe_keys.name: us county level greenhouse gas emissions from irrigation pumping energy 2018 driscoll and co authors 2024

description: This dataset estimates greenhouse gas emissions from the energy used to pump irrigation water in every US county in 2018, split by energy source and by groundwater or surface water. Fuel expenditures for on-farm pumps from the USDA Irrigation and Water Management Survey were combined with fuel prices from the Energy Information Administration and EPA emission factors; the total was 12.6 million tonnes CO2e (90% interval 10.4 to 15.0), mostly from groundwater pumping, with Texas, Nebraska and California giving 46% of the national total, and cleaner electricity grids were projected to cut pumping emissions by 46% by 2050. It was produced by Avery W. Driscoll, Richard T. Conant, Landon T. Marston, Eunkyoung Choi and Nathaniel D. Mueller and published in Nature Communications on 23 January 2024. Coverage is the conterminous US by county. The article is free under CC BY 4.0, and the generated data and code are available to download from a supplementary table and a public repository. Caveats: some crops such as orchards and irrigated pasture were left out, and figures come from survey expenditures, not metered energy. For simulation it gives county-level electricity and fuel demand of irrigation pumps, useful for grid load, fuel supply and climate adaptation scenarios linking farms, water and power. It is related to the USDA NASS Irrigation and Water Management Survey record in this catalogue, its main source. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo record).
